$comment: Source of truth for the stack. scripts/sync.py reads this, pulls each upstream at `ref`, copies the selected paths into plugins/<plugin>, applies the patches and regenerates .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and UPSTREAM.lock.

marketplace.name: frontend-stack
marketplace.description: The frontend design stack for Claude Code: Anthropic frontend-design, Impeccable, UI UX Pro Max, Taste and Emil Kowalski's design engineering skills, curated, de-conflicted and kept in sync.

sources.author: Anthropic
sources.description: Anthropic's official frontend-design skill: distinctive, intentional aesthetic direction instead of templated AI defaults.

sources.author: Anthropic
sources.description: Anthropic's UX research and UX writing skills from the knowledge-work design plugin: plan user research, synthesize findings, write and review interface copy.

sources.author: Paul Bakaus
sources.description: Impeccable by Paul Bakaus: 1 skill with 24 commands (/impeccable polish, audit, critique, harden, ...), design agents, anti-pattern detection hooks.

patches.why: Upstream claims every UI task, including new landing pages, so it loads next to the lead the frontend-stack router picked and starts its own PRODUCT.md interview. Narrowed to its commands.
patches.description: Impeccable design commands for frontend interfaces: plan UX before code (shape), critique, audit, polish, harden, clarify UX copy, adapt, optimize, distill, typeset, colorize, layout, bolder or quieter, delight, onboard, live browser iteration, and design context (init, document, extract). Use when the user asks for one of these, names Impeccable or a /impeccable command, or the frontend-stack router delegates to it. Do not auto-load just to build a new page, landing page or component from scratch: the frontend-stack router picks the lead there. Not for backend-only or non-UI tasks.

sources.author: Next Level Builder
sources.description: UI UX Pro Max: searchable local database of 79 styles, 192 palettes, 74 font pairings, charts and 22 stack guidelines, plus design-system, brand, banner and slides skills.
sources.$comment: Upstream layout (.claude/skills) is kept on purpose: the skill scripts resolve ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/.claude/skills/... and would break if moved.
sources.$comment_patches: Upstream runs `python3 scripts/x.py` relative to the working directory, which is the user's project once installed as a plugin, so the script is not found. ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} is substituted by Claude Code in SKILL.md only, so reference files are left alone.

sources.author: Leonxlnx
sources.description: Taste Skill v2 by Leonxlnx: anti-slop art direction for websites and app screens, with dealt directions, a real-browser inspector and a look-and-fix loop. Needs Node 22 and Chrome, Edge or Chromium.
sources.$comment: Upstream cut this repo down to one skill in v2. The classic presets live in leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics (taste-classics) and the image skills in leonxlnx/imagegen-skills (taste-imagegen). redesign-existing-projects is now part of design-taste-frontend; full-output-enforcement was removed.

sources.author: Leonxlnx
sources.description: Optional. The classic Taste style presets: minimalist, industrial brutalist, high-end 'expensive agency' and Google Stitch DESIGN.md. Opt-in, run by name.
sources.$comment: Excluded on purpose: taste-skill-v1, taste-skill-v2-experimental (superseded by taste) and gpt-tasteskill (tuned for GPT models). Upstream marks every preset disable-model-invocation, which also stops the frontend-stack router from loading them; the patches drop only that key and keep the upstream opt-in descriptions.

patches.why: The router delegates an explicit minimalist look to it; the Skill tool refuses skills with disable-model-invocation.
Same as minimalist-skill: the router delegates an explicit brutalist look to it.
Same as minimalist-skill: the router delegates an explicit 'expensive agency' look to it.
Same as minimalist-skill: the router delegates a Stitch DESIGN.md request to it. It writes DESIGN.md in Stitch format, which collides with Impeccable's, so conflicts.md sends it to DESIGN.stitch.md.

sources.author: Nutlope (Together AI)
sources.description: Hallmark v2 by Nutlope: anti-AI-slop design skill with a hard Floor, 48 themes dealt per prompt, a browser-rendered sloplint and redesign/audit verbs.
sources.$comment: Only skills/hallmark is copied. The edit-time hook (install-hook.mjs) is not wired by the plugin; the user opts in.

patches.why: Upstream writes scripts as node <skill-dir>/scripts/..., a placeholder the agent has to guess once installed as a plugin. ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} is substituted by Claude Code in SKILL.md only.

sources.author: Leonxlnx
sources.description: Optional. Image-first design skills by Leonxlnx (image-to-code, web/mobile design concepts, brand kits). Needs an image-generation tool in your environment.

sources.author: Designed by AI (Sleek)
sources.description: Optional. Design mobile app screens with Sleek and implement them in React Native or HTML. Needs a SLEEK_API_KEY and sends briefs to sleek.design; a free account covers about one trial run, sustained use is paid.

patches.why: Calls a paid third-party API (sleek.design) with the user's brief. Must never fire on a generic mobile UI request; only when Sleek is asked for or the router delegates.
patches.description: Use ONLY when the user asks to design mobile app screens with Sleek, edit a Sleek project, or implement a Sleek design in React Native or HTML, or when the frontend-stack router delegates it. Needs SLEEK_API_KEY and sends the brief to sleek.design (paid service). Not for generic mobile UI work.

sources.author: HeyGen
sources.description: Optional. HyperFrames by HeyGen: write HTML, render deterministic video. For product demos, hero and explainer clips, captions and animated overlays that go with a UI. Needs Node 22 and the hyperframes CLI; some media steps can use HeyGen services.
sources.$comment: Only the four core skills HeyGen publishes. Left out: slideshow (overlaps ui-ux-pro-max slides), figma and remotion-to-hyperframes (off topic). They cross-link with relative paths, so they must stay siblings.

sources.author: Emil Kowalski
sources.description: Emil Kowalski's design engineering skills: UI polish, animation craft (animate, review, improve, find opportunities), Apple-style motion, prototypes, native-feeling mobile web, library picks.

patches.why: Upstream sets disable-model-invocation, so the Skill tool refuses it and the frontend-stack router and ui-reviewer agent cannot load it. Unlocked with a narrow description instead.
patches.description: Use ONLY when the user asks to review motion, or when the frontend-stack router or ui-reviewer agent delegates a motion review. Reviews animation and motion code against a high craft bar derived from Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy. Default to flagging; approval is earned.

patches.why: Same as review-animations: the router delegates library picks to it.
patches.description: Use ONLY when the user asks which library to use, or when the frontend-stack router delegates a library pick. Picks the right library for a frontend task from a curated, opinionated list: numbers, OTP inputs, charts, command menus, virtualization, drag and drop, toasts, state, styling, and more.

patches.why: Same as review-animations: the router delegates multi-version prototypes to it.
patches.description: Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks for several versions of a UI piece to compare, or when the frontend-stack router delegates a comparison of design directions. Builds multiple genuinely different versions behind a visual picker so the user can flip through them live and promote the one that feels right.

sources.author: Emil Kowalski
sources.description: Optional. Emil Kowalski's native skills: React Native / Expo animation and modern Swift.

local_plugins.description: The glue: a router skill that picks the right skill for each frontend task, resolves the rules that conflict between packs, and ships design-director and ui-reviewer agents.
